after_quote.diagnostic (mechanical/local, all three): Retain per-cell alpha histogram and nonzero-alpha component boxes. Flag a component touching all four edges or covering more than half the cell for visual review only. No flag value is an acceptance/rejection threshold; a full-span glyph or deliberate backing can be valid. Alpha-zero RGB is insignificant.
after_quote.visual (visual/visual, all three): Viewed at 1x and 3x nearest on #172336, every frame's intended exterior shows the panel with no unintended opaque canvas matte, tile, halo or fringe. A deliberate backing shape is permitted if part of the recorded subject design with transparent exterior. Partial alpha and selective intentional anti-aliasing are permitted; binary alpha is not required. RGB values where alpha is zero are insignificant. This visual record decides transparency appearance; measured alpha/component flags do not reject artwork.

themes.obligation_change: Owner outcome unchanged: BRIEF.md line 3 'Use transparent backgrounds'. What changed is the route and one restriction. The old rule asked a local mechanical check to decide which pixels are 'outside the marks', which is a subject-construction judgment, and it rejected any 'plate'. The new pair keeps the measurement as a retained diagnostic proxy (flags, no thresholds) and moves the decision to a visual-mode criterion that explicitly permits a deliberate backing shape with transparent exterior and treats alpha-zero RGB as insignificant. Net: route re-scoped to visual; literal rejection narrowed (deliberate plate no longer auto-rejected); no new restriction. The named failure-class examples left the text, but the failed verdicts live.working-animation-01.review.verdict.1 and live.paused-02.review.verdict.1 remain in state.

choices.why_unlinked_is_neither_irrelevant_nor_r: The focused authoring view links choices only through explicit semantic edges (contract ch, decision wr, delivery destinations). A choice outside that graph may still describe the same decision at another time (focused-successor.choice.destination) or an earlier interpretation that the owner later refined (choice.ready). Both remain evidence for reading intent and for checking that a value did not drift. Conversely, inclusion in the index is not a binding: a choice binds a criterion only through a contract that names it, and even then it binds as a choice (proposed/confirmed intent), never as owner authority; request-review.md's authority check applies regardless of link status. So the unlinked records neither need to be ignored nor can they add a rule the linked contracts do not contain.
